not_sufficient_for: broad biological generalization beyond the four paired programs
promotion of unbounded or higher production limits
reasons: All eight paired sessions improved adjudicated function-supported coverage.
All 165 candidate links were independently reviewed twice and all disagreements were adjudicated.
The candidate added two source-opposed claims and failed the cost, latency, and recovery gates.

rows.candidateAdditions: A new mitochondrial mechanism (Chchd6 MICOS/cristae organization, Metap1d N-terminal methionine processing) with no counterpart in the baseline; Explicit Hedgehog pathway signaling mechanism: ciliary GPCR trafficking of Smo/GPR161 as the functional output of Bbs9, Nme7, Tbc1d32; Finer-grained assignment of individual cilia genes to specific subcomplexes (CPLANE, γ-TuRC, IFT-A/B, distal appendages)
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Baseline attributes the cilia module's functional purpose to hemodynamic mechanotransduction (shear-stress sensing), while candidate attributes it to Hedgehog morphogen signaling (Smo/GPR161 export) — these imply different experiments/phenotypes to expect upon perturbation (flow-response assays vs. Shh pathway readouts) and are not presented as complementary; Candidate adds an unrelated mitochondrial cristae/proteostasis mechanism (Chchd6, Metap1d) that changes the perceived functional scope of the program beyond cilia biology; Candidate substantially narrows the regulatory/identity story by dropping Gata2, Eng, and Tet1, leaving only Fzd4 as identity context — a reader would come away with a much thinner view of how this program relates to BBB maintenance and CNS vascular identity
rows.rationale: Both annotations agree the dominant signal is a coherent primary-cilia biogenesis/trafficking module built on the same gene set, situated in postnatal brain endothelium. Beyond that shared core, the two diverge substantively: the candidate replaces the baseline's mechanosensory/shear-stress interpretation of ciliary function with a Hedgehog-signaling (Smo/GPR161 trafficking) interpretation, introduces an unrelated mitochondrial mechanism absent from the baseline, and drops the baseline's regulatory narrative built on Gata2, Eng, and Tet1 (BBB maintenance, TGF-β vascular remodeling, epigenetic angiogenic control), retaining only Fzd4. These are not just added detail or citations — they change what the program is claimed to functionally do (mechanotransduction vs. Hedgehog signaling) and what regulatory genes are implicated in its identity/BBB role, which could lead a reader to prioritize different validation experiments or follow-up hypotheses. This crosses from refinement into material reinterpretation.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow shear stress (KLF2 induction, hemodynamic sensing) — entirely absent from candidate; Gata2 as master endothelial transcription factor / HIF-glycolytic regulator — dropped; Eng/Endoglin as TGF-β co-receptor implicated in HHT and brain AVM risk — dropped; Tet1-mediated epigenetic control of angiogenic gene expression — dropped; CNS vascular identity/BBB maintenance reduced from a full regulatory mechanism (Fzd4+Gata2+Eng+Tet1) to a one-line mention of Fzd4 providing 'cell-type identity context'
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: Primary cilia biogenesis/trafficking machinery (BBSome, IFT-B, transition zone, distal appendages) is the dominant program theme, built from the same core genes: Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Wdpcp, Ift74, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cep164, Nme7; The program is interpreted in the context of mouse brain endothelial cells during postnatal CNS vascular development; Fzd4/Norrin-Wnt signaling is retained as a regulator providing CNS endothelial identity context

rows.candidateAdditions: New secondary mechanism: mitochondrial metabolic maintenance (Bckdhb/BCAA catabolism, Clybl/itaconate-B12, Chchd6/cristae integrity, Metap1d/mito protein processing), linked to Wdpcp's role in mitochondrial biogenesis in ciliated cells; Explicit ciliopathy syndrome framing (Joubert, Meckel, Bardet-Biedl, nephronophthisis, oro-facio-digital) tying the gene cluster to CNS malformation phenotypes; Brief mention of a Hedgehog-signaling role for endothelial cilia in developmental patterning
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Candidate introduces a distinct mitochondrial-metabolism gene set (Bckdhb, Clybl, Chchd6, Metap1d) that could redirect follow-up toward metabolic assays, a hypothesis baseline does not raise; Baseline's specific, testable mechanosensory model (flow-sensing via cilia, KLF2 pathway) is not available to a reader of candidate; Baseline gives pathway-level detail on regulators (Wnt/Norrin, TGF-β/ALK, GATA2-VEGF) useful for choosing a validation target; candidate's regulator treatment is comparatively shallow
rows.rationale: Both annotations agree on the central claim: P10 is a primary-cilia/ciliopathy gene program operating in postnatal brain endothelial cells, with Fzd4/Gata2/Eng regulators framing endothelial identity. The candidate retains this core but adds a genuinely new submechanism (mitochondrial metabolism, supported by a disjoint gene set) and reframes the cilia mechanism toward disease-syndrome annotation rather than the specific mechanosensory/BBB-genesis functional model baseline offered, while also compressing the regulator mechanism into a much thinner treatment. Per the rubric, 'adds a meaningful submechanism' and 'removes/weakens a prior conclusion' are the defining features of same_core_with_meaningful_refinement rather than materially_changed — no existing mechanism is contradicted or reversed, but real gains and losses in mechanistic detail occur across mitochondrial biology (added), endothelial mechanosensing (lost), and vascular regulatory signaling (weakened).
rows.removedOrWeakened: Baseline's dedicated mechanosensing mechanism (cilia as blood-flow shear-stress sensors, KLF2 shear-response amplification, ciliary-length/rapamycin evidence) is absent from candidate; Baseline's fully elaborated regulatory mechanism (Norrin-Wnt-FZD4-β-catenin BBB genesis, ENG/ALK1-ALK5 TGF-β axis and HHT link, GATA2-VEGF sprouting angiogenesis) is reduced to one summary sentence in candidate with no dedicated mechanism entry; Nme7 and Cfap36, cited as ciliome/cilia-associated supporting genes in baseline, are dropped from candidate's explicit ciliary gene list
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: P10 is dominated by a coherent primary-cilia gene cluster (Cc2d2a, Cep164, Ift74, Bbs9, Wdpcp, Tbc1d32, Sdccag8) spanning transition zone, distal appendage, IFT, and BBSome trafficking components; The context is postnatal mouse brain endothelial cells, and primary cilia are functionally relevant to brain vascular development; Perturbation regulators Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng frame the endothelial/vascular identity and signaling backdrop in which the ciliary program operates

rows.candidateAdditions: New standalone mechanism: arteriovenous identity specification (Angpt2 as venous marker repressed by arterial factors, Cxcr4 downregulated at arterial connection, Rgs6 driving Notch-dependent arterial specification) — not present as a distinct theme in baseline; Tnfrsf11b/OPG added as a tip-cell/angiogenic survival gene; Slc1a1/EAAT-3 BBB glutamate-efflux transporter introduced as a program gene with its own mechanistic role; Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 reinterpreted as governing BBB morphogenesis/barrier integrity rather than tip-cell identity
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Baseline attributes the strong Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 KO effect to a documented CNS-specific tip-cell-identity mechanism (ALK5-dependent 'diving' tip cells) with a notable context-reversal relative to peripheral vasculature; candidate attributes the same perturbation to BBB barrier morphogenesis/integrity — these imply different follow-up experiments (angiogenic sprouting/vascular invasion assays vs. barrier permeability assays); Candidate promotes Hopx/Rgs6/Angpt2/Cxcr4 into a distinct arteriovenous-identity program absent from baseline, which would lead a reader toward a different biological framing (AV patterning vs. pure tip-cell sprouting/calcium-mechanosensing); Baseline's calcium-handling/neurovascular-coupling hypothesis (Cacna1c, Jph1, Syt12) is lost, removing a decision-relevant candidate mechanism for functional hyperemia relevance; Introduction of Slc1a1 shifts part of the program's interpretation toward BBB metabolite transport, a functional category absent from baseline
rows.rationale: Both annotations agree on a core tip-cell/angiogenic-sprouting mechanism anchored by Angpt2, Cxcr4, Cdc42ep3, Nrp1, and Tek, and on Kcnj2 as a mechanosensitive channel. However, the candidate replaces baseline's specific, mechanistically distinctive explanation of the Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 requirement (CNS 'diving' tip-cell identity acquisition, notably reversed from peripheral TGF-β biology) with a different explanation (BBB morphogenesis/barrier integrity), drops the calcium-signaling/neurovascular-coupling module (Cacna1c, Jph1, Syt12) entirely, and adds a new arteriovenous-identity-specification mechanism built from genes baseline had assigned elsewhere (Hopx, Rgs6) or interpreted differently (Angpt2, Cxcr4). These are changes to central mechanistic claims, not just added citations or verbosity — a reader would draw different biological conclusions and design different follow-up experiments depending on which version they read, so this exceeds refinement and constitutes a material change.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Baseline's central TGF-β mechanism — CNS-specific 'diving' tip cells uniquely requiring ALK5/Tgfbr1 for tip-cell identity, explicitly opposite to TGF-β's peripheral anti-angiogenic role — is dropped entirely and replaced with a generic BBB-integrity explanation; The calcium-signaling/mechanosensory module (Cacna1c, Jph1, Syt12) linked to neurovascular coupling is entirely absent from the candidate; Prdm1, previously tied to the TGF-β/tip-cell mechanism, is dropped; Gabarapl1 (EPC migration/angiogenesis gene) is dropped from the tip-cell mechanism
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: Angpt2, Cxcr4, Cdc42ep3 with regulators Nrp1/Tek drive tip-cell/angiogenic sprouting behavior in postnatal brain endothelium; Hopx marks a specialized intracranial arterial EC state; Kcnj2/Kir2.1 functions as a flow/mechanosensitive endothelial K+ channel; Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 knockouts both decrease the program (TGF-β receptor signaling required)

rows.candidateAdditions: New mechanosensitive flow-sensing theme built around Kcnj2 (Kir2.1) shear-stress response, absent from baseline; New endothelial survival/anti-apoptotic theme via Tnfrsf11b (OPG)-TRAIL blockade and tube formation, absent from baseline; New metabolic-support theme via Slc1a1-mediated metabolite influx fueling mitochondrial respiration, absent from baseline; Rgs6 added as a tip-cell/Notch-arterial gene not mentioned in baseline; Explicit 'evidence gap' designation for many program/distinctive genes (Hopx, Prdm1, Ctdspl, Cacna1c, Chst9, Syt12, Jph1, Rhod, Bag2, Epb41l4b, Gabarapl1)
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Baseline treats arterial specification (Dll4-Notch-CXCR4-Hopx) as one of three co-equal core mechanisms; candidate removes this axis and explicitly denies evidentiary support for its key marker (Hopx), so a reader would no longer conclude P11 marks arterial EC identity; Baseline attributes program regulation to a specific TGF-β→Angpt2 repression homeostatic mechanism; candidate discards this specific regulatory logic and instead attributes the Tgfbr1/2 regulator effect to a generic supportive role bundled with unrelated survival/metabolism genes (Tnfrsf11b, Slc1a1); Candidate introduces mechanosensitive hemodynamic flow-sensing (Kcnj2) as a full third mechanism, a functional category entirely absent from baseline, which would lead a reader to a different functional hypothesis about what drives program activity
rows.rationale: Only one of three central mechanisms (tip-cell/sprouting angiogenesis via Angpt2, Cxcr4, Nrp1) is substantively shared, and even that mechanism drops a supporting gene (Cdc42ep3) and adds another (Rgs6). The other two baseline mechanisms — Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 arterial specification anchored by Hopx, and TGF-β-mediated Angpt2 repression for vascular integrity — are dropped or reduced to vague, non-mechanistic statements; Hopx's role is explicitly reversed from 'confirmed arterial marker' to 'evidence gap.' In their place, candidate introduces two entirely new mechanisms (Kcnj2 flow-sensing; Tnfrsf11b/Slc1a1 survival-metabolism) built on genes never discussed in baseline. This is not additional detail on the same story but a different set of central mechanisms, satisfying materially_changed.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 arteriovenous specification axis dropped as a standalone mechanism; Hopx as a marker confirming intracranial arterial EC identity is reversed: candidate flags it as lacking direct published evidence in brain endothelial contexts; Prdm1's supporting role in the Notch-arterial axis dropped, now listed as an evidence gap; Cdc42ep3 dropped as supporting evidence for Nrp1-CDC42-filopodia link; Specific TGF-β-mediated repression of Angpt2 and vascular-integrity mechanism (Tgfbr1/2 KO hemorrhage, Alk1/Alk5-Smad2/3 pathway) replaced by a generic, unmechanistic statement that TGF-β 'supports brain vascular development and angiogenic capacity'
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: P11 reflects postnatal brain endothelial tip-cell identity / sprouting angiogenesis; Angpt2 and Cxcr4 are core tip-cell marker genes; Nrp1 acts as a regulator promoting tip-cell filopodia formation via CDC42; Tek is retained as a supporting regulator of the angiogenic axis

rows.candidateAdditions: Rdh11 introduced as a novel SREBP2-regulated hepatocyte cholesterol-homeostasis gene (induced by statins, reduced by high-fat/cholesterol diet, co-regulated with Hmgcr/Ldlr) — a gene not mentioned anywhere in the baseline; Erg28 given an explicit functional assignment as the non-catalytic scaffold of the C4-demethylation complex, SREBP2 co-regulated, whose loss impairs SREBP2 activation (baseline only listed Erg28 as a supporting gene without functional detail); Four distinctive genes (Ddr2, Cetn2, Zfp839, Tas2r138) explicitly flagged as having no retrieved evidence linking them to the pathway; Gene-specific phenotype evidence added: hepatocyte Cyp51 knockout causes liver injury/oval-cell response/fibrosis; Tm7sf2 deficiency causes lipid accumulation and ER stress in regenerating liver; Mechanistic detail that Acss2 acts independently of Acly and that dual Acss2+Acly inhibition is needed to suppress hepatic lipogenesis; Mechanistic detail on Mttp-Acat2 interaction: Mttp relieves product inhibition of Acat2-mediated cholesteryl ester synthesis, linking esterification to VLDL export; Quantitative detail that Scap knockout reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis by ~80%; MASLD/NASH-specific detail that dysregulated Scap:Insig1 ratios drive free cholesterol accumulation
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Rdh11 as a newly asserted SREBP2 target gene could prompt follow-up validation or inclusion in the gene program that baseline did not suggest; Erg28's clarified mechanistic role (scaffold vs. undefined supporting gene) changes how a reader would prioritize it for functional follow-up; Explicit non-evidence flag for Ddr2/Cetn2/Zfp839/Tas2r138 helps a reader triage which distinctive genes still need investigation, which baseline left implicit
rows.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same central biological story: P21 is the hepatic de novo cholesterol biosynthesis pathway under SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional control, balanced against Ldlr-mediated uptake, fed by Acss2-derived acetyl-CoA, and coupled to Dgat2/Mttp-driven VLDL-TG export in the MASLD context. No mechanism, direction, or regulatory relationship is reversed or contradicted. The candidate's value-add is (1) a new gene-function claim (Rdh11 as an SREBP2 target), (2) a specific mechanistic role for Erg28 that was previously just a listed gene, (3) explicit acknowledgment of unexplained distinctive genes, and (4) denser gene-specific and context-specific literature support (KO phenotypes, Acss2/Acly relationship, Mttp-Acat2 interaction, quantitative Scap effect size). These are meaningful refinements and gene-function assignments layered onto an unchanged core interpretation, not a change in the program's biological identity or the direction of any regulatory effect.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Baseline's broader 'aging and MASLD' framing for the Dgat2/Mttp coupling mechanism is narrowed in the candidate to MASLD/NASH context only, dropping the aging reference
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: P21 is the near-complete mevalonate-pathway/post-squalene de novo cholesterol biosynthesis program in mouse hepatocytes (Hmgcs1 through Dhcr7, plus Acat2 esterification); Program transcription is gated by the SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback circuit: Scap knockout abrogates the program, Insig1 knockout hyperactivates it; Ldlr knockout drives compensatory upregulation of de novo synthesis, forming the uptake/synthesis balance limb; Acss2 supplies acetyl-CoA substrate for the pathway; Dgat2 and Mttp couple cholesterol synthesis to VLDL-triglyceride assembly/export, relevant to hepatic lipid handling in MASLD

rows.candidateAdditions: Explicit two-arm structure (mevalonate arm vs post-squalene sterol arm) with defined enzyme order; Erg28 reassigned a specific molecular role as non-catalytic scaffold binding Nsdhl/Msmo1 in the C4-demethylation complex, plus a feedback claim that Erg28 loss impairs SREBP-2 activation; Direct SRE promoter-binding evidence added for Erg28, Dhcr7, and distinctive gene Rdh11, sharpening the transcriptional-control mechanism from 'controls the pathway' to 'binds these specific promoters'; New distinctive gene Ddr2 introduced with a specific anti-steatotic AMPK/ACC mechanism in MASLD liver; Fads2 added as a regulator linking PUFA synthesis/lipogenesis to the lipid-homeostasis context
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Baseline points a reader toward senescence/ERRα/mitochondrial dysfunction as the aging-relevant downstream consequence of this program; candidate offers no support for that and instead proposes an anti-steatotic Ddr2/AMPK-ACC axis as the MASLD-relevant context, a different follow-up hypothesis; Candidate's scaffold (not enzyme) role for Erg28, with a bidirectional Erg28-SREBP2 feedback claim, changes what kind of validation experiment (complex/structural vs enzymatic) would be prioritized for that gene; Candidate supplies specific SRE promoter-binding claims (Erg28, Dhcr7, Rdh11) giving more direct transcriptional mechanistic evidence than baseline's generic 'SREBP2 controls this gene set'; Dropping Ldlr means a reader using only the candidate loses the uptake-arm component of the transcriptional circuit that baseline described
rows.rationale: Both annotations agree P21 is the mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program under SCAP/Insig1/SREBP2 control with the same enzyme roster and the same MASLD-linked regulators (Dgat2, Mttp) — the central interpretation is preserved. The candidate meaningfully refines this with gene-specific mechanistic claims (Erg28 as scaffold with feedback to SREBP2, direct SRE sites for three genes) and extends the MASLD arm with a new gene (Ddr2) and regulator (Fads2). It also drops two baseline claims (Ldlr as uptake arm; senescence/ERRα/mitochondrial link in aging) without replacing them with an aging-relevant mechanism, which is a real narrowing of the disease-context narrative but does not alter the program's core enzymatic/regulatory identity. This pattern — retained core, added gene-function detail, one context-level mechanism reframed/removed — matches 'same_core_with_meaningful_refinement' rather than a material change to the program's central interpretation.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Ldlr as the SREBP2-driven cholesterol-uptake arm of the circuit is dropped entirely from the candidate; Baseline's aging/senescence claim (mevalonate pathway overactivity drives hepatic cellular senescence via the ERRα/mitochondrial axis) is removed and not replaced with any aging-related claim
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: P21 is a near-complete transcriptional program for de novo mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis in hepatocytes, covering essentially the same enzyme set (Hmgcs1, Idi1, Mvk, Pmvk, Mvd, Fdps, Fdft1, Lss, Cyp51, Msmo1, Nsdhl, Hsd17b7, Tm7sf2, Sc5d, Dhcr7, Erg28); Acss2 supplies acetyl-CoA as pathway carbon source and Acat2 esterifies cholesterol; Scap and Insig1 form the ER-anchored SREBP2 toggle that transcriptionally controls the whole enzyme set; Dgat2 and Mttp connect VLDL/triglyceride handling to the program in the MASLD disease context

rows.candidateAdditions: Htatip2 added as a hepatic fatty acid storage/oxidation regulator; More specific enzyme assignments: Cyp2c50 as arachidonic-acid/EET epoxygenase, Sult2a8 as the PPARalpha-regulated major 7alpha-OH bile acid sulfotransferase, Sord placed in the polyol-fructose pathway; New standalone bile acid biotransformation mechanism pairing Sult2a8 sulfonation with Cdo1 taurine conjugation and cholesterol handling; Transcription-factor regulatory context (Nrf2, CAR, PXR, PPARalpha) for the detox battery
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Baseline affirms P25 supports hepatic ammonia/nitrogen disposal via the urea cycle (Car5a->CPS1 bicarbonate, Agmat); candidate provides no basis for this, giving a reader the opposite answer to whether the program handles nitrogen/ammonia detoxification; Cdo1's pathway attribution shifts from general sulfur/nitrogen catabolism to bile acid taurine conjugation, changing which functional axis a reader assigns the gene to; Loss of urea-cycle/nitrogen context regulators (G6pc, Insr) removes the evidence anchoring the dropped nitrogen-disposal theme
rows.rationale: Both annotations share the dominant frame of a pericentral hepatocyte program coupling Phase I/II detoxification, bile acid/steroid processing, and lipid-droplet/peroxisomal fatty-acid metabolism in an aging/MASLD context, and the candidate genuinely refines the retained themes with gene-specific detail (EET epoxygenase, PPARalpha-regulated Sult2a8, Htatip2, Sord polyol pathway) and TF context. However, the candidate does not merely trim citations or qualify an existing conclusion: it eliminates one of the three named central mechanisms in the baseline — sulfur amino acid catabolism feeding hepatic nitrogen/ammonia disposal and urea-cycle support, built on Cdo1+Car5a+Agmat. Car5a and Agmat disappear entirely, and Cdo1 is re-attributed to a bile acid taurine-conjugation axis. This is an affirmative, biologically distinct functional claim (ammonia/urea handling) that a reader of the candidate would no longer draw, and Cdo1's pathway reassignment changes attribution of a shared gene. Because a reader could reach a different biological decision about whether P25 participates in nitrogen/ammonia detoxification, this exceeds refinement and constitutes a material change to a central program mechanism. This resolves the prior disagreement in favor of the materially_changed call: the secondary assessor correctly identified the same removals but under-weighted that the removed item was a distinctly named central mechanism carrying an independent functional conclusion, not a peripheral qualifier.
rows.removedOrWeakened: Entire nitrogen/ammonia disposal (urea cycle support) mechanism removed: Car5a (bicarbonate to CPS1) and Agmat (agmatine/arginine polyamine-urea handling) absent from all candidate mechanisms; Cdo1 reassigned from sulfur amino acid catabolism/nitrogen disposal to bile acid taurine conjugation; Lonp2 (peroxisomal Lon protease, oxidized-protein clearance) dropped; Sult2a5 and Sult2a7 downgraded from credited detox members to unsupported 'likely paralog' mentions; Perturbation regulators Tpst1, Insig1, G6pc, and Insr dropped
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: Coordinated Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification battery (Cyp2c50, Aldh1a1, Aldh3a2, Gsta3, Akr1c6) characteristic of pericentral hepatocytes; Bile acid/steroid sulfation via SULT2A enzymes supports biliary/urinary elimination; Lipid droplet biogenesis (Fitm1) coupled to peroxisomal/ER fatty acid oxidation (Eci2, Hao2, Cyb5b); Cdo1 channels cysteine catabolism toward taurine production; Program interpreted in a pericentral hepatocyte aging/MASLD context

rows.candidateAdditions: Sult2a8 specifically called out as the major mouse liver 7α-OH bile acid sulfotransferase (sharper gene-function assignment); New Psmd1 proteasome-mediated mechanism regulating hepatocellular lipid droplet accumulation via p38-JNK/AKT signaling; Aldh1a1 connected to NAFLD-relevant vitamin A/retinaldehyde metabolism; Cdo1 linked to coenzyme A synthesis balance as an added downstream consequence
rows.decisionRelevantDifferences: Loss of the Nrf2/CAR regulatory framing changes how upstream transcriptional control of the detox module would be interpreted; Dropping Cyp2c50 shifts mechanism 1 from a combined phase I/II oxidative-and-conjugative program to a purely phase II sulfation/conjugation program; Addition of Psmd1 introduces a distinct post-translational (proteasome-mediated) regulatory route for lipid droplet accumulation not present in the baseline; Removing the Cdo1-gluconeogenesis link changes the claimed physiological consequence of Cdo1 activity from glucose output control to CoA synthesis balance
rows.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same three-theme architecture (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation/lipid droplet handling, sulfur/nitrogen catabolism with an aging signature) and rely on largely overlapping gene sets and regulators, so the core biological identity of P25 is unchanged. However, the candidate drops the baseline's explicit Nrf2/CAR transcriptional-regulation narrative and the Cyp2c50 phase I enzyme, swaps Eci2/Lonp2 for a new Psmd1 proteasome-lipogenesis mechanism, and replaces the cited Cdo1-gluconeogenesis link with a CoA-synthesis claim. These are meaningful gene-function and mechanistic refinements/losses rather than a wholesale reinterpretation, placing this at same_core_with_meaningful_refinement with mixed evidence depth change (gains in some gene-specific detail, losses in regulatory/mechanistic specificity elsewhere).
rows.removedOrWeakened: Nrf2/CAR nuclear receptor transcriptional coordination of the Phase I/II detox module (including CAR-Mrp4 cholestasis-protective link) is dropped from mechanism 1; Cyp2c50, a cytochrome P450 (phase I) gene, is removed entirely from the candidate's mechanistic coverage; Eci2 (unsaturated fatty acid beta-oxidation) and Lonp2 (peroxisomal protein quality control) are dropped from the fatty acid oxidation mechanism; Agmat (agmatinase, urea/polyamine pathway) is dropped from the sulfur/nitrogen mechanism; The specific Cdo1-to-gluconeogenesis mechanistic claim (CDO1 knockdown raises liver cysteine and glucose output, PMID 39819116) is dropped
rows.sharedCoreConclusions: Program organizes into three themes: bile acid/hydroxysteroid Phase II sulfation, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation with lipid droplet handling, and sulfur amino acid catabolism/metabolic aging; SULT2A family (Sult2a5/7/8) plus Gsta3/Akr1c6/Aldh1a1 drive Phase II detoxification of bile acids and steroids; Hao2, Aldh3a2, Fitm1 (and Cyb5b) support peroxisomal/microsomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid aldehyde/triglyceride handling; Cdo1 is the rate-limiting, bile acid/FXR-regulated cysteine dioxygenase feeding taurine and GSH synthesis; Rgn/SMP30 marks hepatocyte aging decline; Car5a and Alad extend the program into urea cycle/heme synthesis support; Regulators Insig1, Abcg5, G6pc, Dgat2 tie the program to hepatic lipid/sterol/glucose homeostasis and MASLD relevance

rows.baselineClaimedButNotAudited: Cacna1c, Cdc42ep3, Jph1, Prdm1, Rgs6, Syt12
Agmat, Akr1c6, Cyb5b, Eci2, Hao2, Sord, Sult2a5, Sult2a7, Sult2a8
Akr1c6, Alad, Eci2, Lonp2, Sult2a5, Sult2a7, Sult2a8

anchors.0.50: same broad process but different central mechanism or output

method.description: Two independent assessors score all nine module pairs on a 0–1 semantic scale; cell scores are averaged and the best one-to-one assignment is selected from the six possible permutations.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly

matching.leftName: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
matching.rightName: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells

matching.leftName: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
matching.rightName: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation

rows.primaryRationale: This is a near-identical baseline replicate: the cilia biogenesis module (L1/R1), endothelial cilia mechanosensing module (L2/R2), and Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng regulator module (L3/R3) each match one-to-one with near-perfect similarity, while cross-pairs share genes/tissue context but diverge in core mechanism (structural biogenesis vs. mechanosensory function vs. transcriptional regulation), warranting low partial-overlap or context-only scores.
rows.secondaryRationale: The replicates contain three strongly corresponding programs: core ciliogenesis, endothelial ciliary mechanosensing, and FZD4/GATA2/ENG-mediated CNS vascular-barrier regulation, with weaker cross-pair overlap driven mainly by ciliary dependence or shared brain-endothelial context.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia assembly: IFT machinery, distal appendages, CPLANE module, and transition zone organization
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis, transition zone organization, and intraflagellar transport

matching.leftName: BBSome-mediated ciliary GPCR trafficking and Hedgehog pathway regulation
matching.rightName: (no module reported)

matching.leftName: Mitochondrial inner membrane organization and protein biogenesis
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial metabolic function: BCAA catabolism, cristae integrity, and co-factor metabolism

rows.primaryRationale: The two replicates largely converge: a near-identical ciliary structural assembly module (L1≈R1), a mitochondrial proteostasis/cristae module that R2 refines with added metabolic genes (L3≈R2), while L2's Hedgehog/GPCR-signaling-output module is only partially captured inside R1's broader assembly framing and the right set is missing a third distinct module.
rows.secondaryRationale: Both sets reproduce the primary-cilium assembly and mitochondrial programs, while the replicate folds ciliary signaling into its broader ciliogenesis module and reports no third module.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis and ciliary trafficking via BBSome, IFT, and transition zone machinery
matching.rightName: Primary cilia assembly: IFT machinery, distal appendages, CPLANE module, and transition zone organization

matching.leftName: Endothelial primary cilia as mechanosensors for blood flow in brain vasculature
matching.rightName: BBSome-mediated ciliary GPCR trafficking and Hedgehog pathway regulation

matching.leftName: CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier maintenance via Norrin/Wnt-Fzd4 signaling, GATA2, and Endoglin
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial inner membrane organization and protein biogenesis

rows.primaryRationale: Both settings decompose the cilia biology into a broad structural-assembly module (L1≈R1, strong same_core match) and a narrower functional/signaling module, but the right setting's second cilia module (R2) centers on BBSome-Hedgehog GPCR trafficking whereas the left's second module (L2) centers on endothelial mechanosensation of blood flow, giving only partial overlap across that pairing in both directions; the left's third module is a Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng BBB angiogenesis program while the right's third module is an unrelated mitochondrial proteostasis cluster, so these have essentially no correspondence except a shared Fzd4 regulator touching R1 and weak tissue-context ties to R3.
rows.secondaryRationale: The strongest correspondence is the shared primary-cilium assembly machinery, while ciliary mechanosensing, Hedgehog trafficking, BBB regulation, and mitochondrial organization represent distinct outputs or mechanisms despite some endothelial context overlap.

matching.leftName: Primary cilia biogenesis: basal body docking, transition zone integrity, intraflagellar transport, and BBSome assembly
matching.rightName: Primary cilia biogenesis, transition zone organization, and intraflagellar transport

matching.leftName: Primary cilia mechanosensing and blood-brain barrier maturation in brain endothelial cells
matching.rightName: Mitochondrial metabolic function: BCAA catabolism, cristae integrity, and co-factor metabolism

matching.leftName: Wnt/Norrin-FZD4 signaling and endothelial identity regulators governing BBB and CNS vascular barrier formation
matching.rightName: (no module reported)

rows.primaryRationale: Both sets share a near-identical core ciliary biogenesis module (L1/R1), but the right set's second module pivots to mitochondrial metabolism while the left set's second and third modules focus on endothelial mechanosensing and Wnt/transcriptional regulators, and the right set has no third module at all, so only one strong cross-module match exists.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly agree on primary-cilium construction, while the candidate replaces the baseline's endothelial mechanosensing and vascular signaling modules with mitochondrial metabolism and one missing module.

rows.primaryRationale: The two sets share a clear structural correspondence: module 1 in each set is the core mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthetic enzyme cascade (near-identical), module 2 in each set is the SCAP-INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional control axis (same core with differing refinements), and module 3 in each set extends into MASLD-linked lipid dysregulation sharing Dgat2/Mttp regulators (same core with differing submechanisms — aging/senescence vs. esterification/Ddr2); off-diagonal pairs show only weak contextual overlap via shared regulators or a single gene without shared central mechanism.
rows.secondaryRationale: The sets strongly agree on the enzymatic cholesterol-biosynthesis and SCAP–SREBP2–INSIG1 control modules, while their MASLD modules overlap in lipid-homeostasis context but emphasize different mechanisms and outcomes.

rows.primaryRationale: The two module sets are strongly congruent one-to-one: L1↔R1 (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation/conjugation), L2↔R2 (peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis), and L3↔R3 (cysteine/taurine/sulfur-nitrogen catabolism with hepatocyte aging signature) each share core mechanism, dominant genes, and key regulators, while all cross-pairs are biologically distinct processes linked only by incidental shared regulators or a single overlapping gene with divergent roles.
